nodes.description: ISalt public state variable holding the external ISalt interface instance used by tokenURI
Constructor(address a) that casts the supplied address to ISalt and writes it into state variable salt
Public view tokenURI(uint256) that branches on salt.startDate() and computes a shifted token id using block.timestamp
block.timestamp, miner/validator influenced value used directly in the day calculation
Unchecked arithmetic ((block.timestamp - salt.startDate()) % 180 days) / 1 days; underflows if startDate() > block.timestamp and is timestamp dependent
Unchecked arithmetic (tokenId + daysPassed) % 180; addition can overflow uint256 and wraps silently in Solidity 0.6.8
External calls to the interface target salt (startDate() and rawURI()), executed before the return value is produced
Address parameter a of the constructor, converted to ISalt
uint256 tokenId parameter of tokenURI, feeds the unchecked addition
Local uint256 daysPassed derived from timestamp arithmetic and added to tokenId

edges.reason: Constructor parameter a is bound to the constructor execution scope
Constructor parameter a is cast to ISalt and stored into state variable salt
Constructor writes the salt state variable
tokenURI reads the salt state variable to invoke startDate() and rawURI()
block.timestamp is subtracted from salt.startDate() in unchecked integer arithmetic
tokenURI output depends on the miner-influenceable block.timestamp
daysPassed is assigned the result of the unchecked timestamp arithmetic
daysPassed is added to tokenId without overflow checking
tokenId takes part in the unchecked addition with daysPassed
daysPassed is used to derive the token id passed to salt.rawURI
tokenId is passed as argument to salt.rawURI
tokenURI invokes the external salt interface functions startDate() and rawURI()
Control returns from the external ISalt call back into tokenURI; salt address is fixed at construction so no state-changing reentrancy is possible in a view function
The timestamp arithmetic statement is executed inside tokenURI
The tokenId addition statement is executed inside tokenURI
tokenId is the input parameter of tokenURI
daysPassed local variable is declared and used inside tokenURI

normalization_plan.reason: Constructor parameter a is only used to cast and initialize the salt state variable, so it can be folded into the constructor function node
tokenURI parameter tokenId only flows into the unchecked (tokenId + daysPassed) arithmetic, so it can be merged into the arithmetic unsafe operation
daysPassed is a temporary local computed directly from the unchecked timestamp arithmetic and can be absorbed into that unsafe operation
